candidate_segment_count_conservation.explanation: filtered_claim_count is NOT a third disjoint bucket alongside retained_claim_count -- it deliberately re-includes non_substantive_removed_count as one of its 3 summed components (see comqutor_alpha/structure_engine/structured_output_adapter.py adapt_run_outputs: retained_claim_count = candidate_segment_count - non_substantive_removed_count; filtered_claim_count = boilerplate_removed_count + disclaimer_removed_count + non_substantive_removed_count). The naive retained+filtered formula double-counts non_substantive_removed_count and is therefore NOT the correct conservation law; the two formulas above are, and both hold exactly for this run. This is a documentation/API-shape subtlety, not a computation defect.

candidate_edges_vs_admitted_plus_rejecte.note: candidate_edges != admitted_edges + rejected_edges is EXPECTED here: candidate_edges is claim-level (21, keyed per-claim), admitted_edges is run-level POST-MERGE (9, keyed by (source,target,edge_type) with duplicates from multiple claims collapsed into one edge) -- graph_builder's own rejected_edges counter (self_loop/dangling/invalid_type/invalid_weight) is a THIRD, separate axis (malformed-input rejections, not duplicate-merge). See graph_metrics.rejected_edges below for the real rejection breakdown.
candidate_edges_vs_admitted_plus_rejecte.reconciliation: candidate_edge_count (21) - distinct (source,target,edge_type) keys after per-claim dedup = admitted_edge_count (9); the arithmetic gap (12) is claim-level duplicate MERGES at graph_builder's run-level (source,target,edge_type) key, not rejections -- run_audit_rejected_edge_count_field correctly reports 0 true structural rejections, matching graph_metrics.rejected_edges all-zero.

raw_agent_output_count.note: all 12 raw agent outputs were successfully processed (0 explicit failures) -- structured_output_adapter never emits a NO_MEANINGFUL_CLAIMS placeholder for any of the 12 agents this run.

conflict_count_field_semantics.note: run_audit.json's conflict_count counts ADMITTED conflicts only (3); it does NOT surface declared_pair_count(6)/suppressed_count(1)/rejected_count(2) as explicit top-level fields -- that full arbitration detail exists only in the alpha_conflicts DB table's outcome column, not in run_audit.json itself. This is a completeness gap in run_audit's own schema, not a correctness error.
